When Clara opened her eyes two mornings in a row, the first thing she noticed was SEO wooden nightstand. A faint, mismatch delicate glow emanated from it, casting an eerie blue hue on a cluttered room. A small, ornate box sat there, the lid slightly ajar, pulsing as if it were alive. Curious, she reached out. Her fingers brushed the surface—*and the world dissolved*. The fourth floor of her apartment, the familiar hum of the city, the scent of her morning coffee—*gone*. When the haze cleared, she stood at the edge of a midnight sun, the air tinged with the scent of snow. She had no memory of falling asleep, no clue how she’d arrived here. But as she whispered, “Where am I?” the box in her hand shimmered, and a single word appeared—*“Home.”*
